nonBlockingNotes: AC8 channel (residuals on PR body vs comment) is decided as 'PR body via gh api PATCH' in Delta/AC8, yet OQ4 re-opens the same body-vs-comment question. The coverage is present (a concrete channel is chosen), but the design carries an internal tension between a committed decision and an open question on the same point — worth resolving before Structure. Non-blocking for completeness.

The design lacks an explicit 'Out of Scope' section mirroring the ticket's (RUS-94, RUS-59, RUS-90, plan/impl gates). These are exclusions rather than requirements-to-cover, so this is not a coverage gap; the 'Design phase only' framing and Risk Register implicitly honor them. Calling them out explicitly would aid the Structure phase.

AC8 vs OQ4 channel tension (non-material). AC8 asserts the residual findings on cap-exhaustion are 'attached to the PR body via `gh api … pulls/<N> -X PATCH`', a decided channel. OQ4 reopens it: 'Does the human-facing residual attachment go in the PR body (via `gh api … PATCH`) or as a comment — AC8 says "attached to the PR" … confirm the channel.' This is softer than a flat contradiction because OQ4 is reading AC8's looser 'attached to the PR' wording as the ambiguity it flags rather than negating a concrete build instruction, but a reviser may still find AC8 and OQ4 disagree on whether the channel is settled.

Inverted config default is internally consistent but knowingly diverges from the codebase convention. AC10 ('enabled default true'), the Delta (`resolve_enabled(cfg, True)`), and the Risk Register all agree the gate defaults ON, so there is no internal contradiction. The design itself notes this inverts the uniform opt-in (default OFF) convention that the research (Q6/Q10) records; that is a fidelity/convention concern for other lenses, not an internal-consistency defect — flagged only so it is not mistaken for a self-contradiction.

All other cross-references resolve cleanly: the persist `ARTIFACTS` enum, `synthesize` returning `{pass, findings}`, the `resolve_enabled(cfg, default)` signature, the reviser's dormant/scratch-only contract, and the absent (correctly 'New agent') verifier were all confirmed against source; and the load-bearing contract shapes (gate return `{converged, rounds, residualFindings, logPath}`, AC4 reduce `{pass, residualFindings}`, AC5/Decision-3 reviser staging-path → `qrspi_persist.py --artifact design`) agree in every appearance within the design.

AC8 residual-attachment channel: the design picks the PR-body PATCH (gh api ... pulls/<N> -X PATCH) as the mechanism in Desired End State (line 27) yet correctly flags the body-vs-comment ambiguity as OQ4. This is faithful to the ticket (AC8 only says 'attached to the PR') and to research Q11 (PATCH-body is the established post-creation mechanism, and gate mode otherwise posts no comment), so it is not a drift — but the design asserts the body channel in one place while leaving it open in another. A reviser may want to reconcile that minor internal tension before it propagates to Structure.

AC10 inverted config default (enabled: true) is a deliberate, ticket-mandated departure from the codebase's uniform opt-in (default-OFF) convention documented in research Q6/Q10/Discovered-Patterns. The design grounds it correctly (ticket AC10 + the maintainer quality-over-cost mandate) and flags the divergence explicitly in the Delta and Risk Register, so it is aligned, not unsupported drift — noting it only because it is the one place the design intentionally contradicts an established codebase convention.

AC3 (cross-critic debate) layers a bespoke dissent-preserving stabilization core (vote agree/dispute, a finding survives if any lens defends it, majority-dispute drops only findings no lens defends) on top of AC4's reduce, which reuses `synthesize`. Research Q5 shows `synthesize` already returns the deduped UNION of every lens's findings — i.e., it already preserves any finding any lens raised. The debate machinery's only net effect beyond that union is to DROP a finding when its originating lens recants its own vote, a narrow case. The debate itself is ticket-mandated ('~3 exchanges', OQ2), so this is not blocking, but the design could note that the dissent-preservation outcome largely coincides with the existing union reducer and justify why the additional drop-by-vote core earns its keep over just unioning findings each round.

The design is large (12 ACs, 4 pattern decisions, 5+ modified files, 3 new pure cores, 1 new agent), but the ticket scope (a full work->review->revise->verify->converge loop with debate, committed log, config, and publish-with-residuals) is itself inherently multi-part, and ACs map nearly 1:1 to ticket requirements. Decisions 1-4 each reuse existing mechanisms (the engine's mode-dispatch, the JS<->Python worker seam, Fix-A persist verbatim, `build_record`/`synthesize`) and explicitly answer 'NEW PATTERN? No' with a defensible rationale. The proportionality is therefore broadly sound apart from the verifier finding above.

The gate seam runs BEFORE any design PR exists. Research Q1 confirms 'no PR yet exists for the design branch' at the post-design/pre-finalize insertion point, and AC8 confirms the PR is only submitted at Finalize (after the gate). But the existing qrspi-review Resolve worker hard-requires an existing phase PR: it derives the PR via `gh pr list --head <ticket>/design --json number` and returns `ok:false` ('the design phase PR does not exist') when none is found (.claude/workflows/qrspi-review.js:257, :289-293), then snapshots a head SHA. The design's Decision 1 Option A reuses 'shared resolve/panel/reduce helpers' and the Delta for runGateMode only calls out skipping the comment write and the SHA re-assert block — it never states that gate mode must bypass or replace the PR-derivation + SHA-snapshot in Resolve. As written, a literal reuse of the shared Resolve worker in gate mode would abort with ok:false because no PR exists yet. This is a design-completeness gap (resolvable at structure/plan altitude), not a false codebase claim — surfacing it so the next phase wires a PR-free resolve path for gate mode.

The panel fan-out hardcodes the lens subject at the scratch copy: every lens prompt emits `${cfg.subjectVar} = ${resolved.scratch}` (qrspi-review.js:306, :333) and `resolved.scratch` is produced by the Resolve worker's `cp <worktree>/.qrspi/<id>/design.md /tmp/phase-stage/<id>/review/design.md` step (:272-275). AC1 says gate 'operates on the real worktree design.md (not the scratch copy)'. These are reconcilable (gate can re-copy worktree→scratch each round so each panel round reads a fresh copy of the just-revised worktree file), but the design does not spell out how the per-round panel re-reads the freshly-persisted worktree artifact given the panel's hardcoded scratch binding. A worth-noting detail for the structure/plan phase, not a blocker.

AC9 commits `design-review-log.md` 'alongside the design artifacts in the design commit', but the design Finalize worker today stages ONLY questions.md/research.md/design.md and verifies exactly those three exist non-empty before committing (qrspi-batch.js:716-717). The Delta acknowledges extending the Finalize stage-and-commit set, but note the Finalize prompt also has an explicit 3-artifact existence precheck ('Verify questions.md, research.md, design.md exist... If any missing/empty, return ok:false') that the gate-on-non-convergence path must keep tolerant — the log is an additional file, and a missing log should not be conflated with a missing producer artifact.

OQ1/Decision 4: gate-mode ledger row. If gate writes a `critic-metrics.jsonl` row, note that `build_record` -> qrspi_critic_metrics validates terminal_action against VALID_TERMINAL_ACTIONS and rejects non-terminal values; the gate's convergence/cap evaluator emits `converged|continue|exhausted` (AC7) where `continue` is a per-round intermediate, not a terminal action — only the FINAL action (converged/exhausted/cap_reached) is record-valid. A non-terminal action reaching build_record would raise. This is internal to the new cores but worth flagging so the gate only persists a terminal action to the ledger.
